name: std::ranges::is_sorted

declarations.code:
template <ranges::forward_range R, class Proj = std::identity,

    std::indirect_strict_weak_order<

        std::projected<ranges::iterator_t<R>, Proj>>

        Comp = ranges::less>

constexpr bool

is_sorted(R &&r, Comp comp = {}, Proj proj = {});

intro:
Checks if the elements in range [first, last) are sorted in non-descending order.

A sequence is sorted with respect to a comparator comp if for any iterator it pointing to the sequence and any non-negative integer n such that it + n is a valid iterator pointing to an element of the sequence, std::invoke(comp, std::invoke(proj, *(it + n)), std::invoke(proj, *it)) evaluates to false.

1) Elements are compared using the given binary comparison function comp.

2) Same as (1), but uses r as the source range, as if using ranges::begin(r) as first and ranges::end(r) as last.

The function-like entities described on this page are algorithm function objects (informally known as niebloids), that is:

Explicit template argument lists cannot be specified when calling any of them.
 None of them are visible to argument-dependent lookup.
 When any of them are found by normal unqualified lookup as the name to the left of the function-call operator, argument-dependent lookup is inhibited.

sections.title: Parameters
sections.text:
first, last

 -

 iterator-sentinel defining the range to check if it is sorted


 r

 -

 the range to check if it is sorted


 comp

 -

 comparison function to apply to the projected elements


 proj

 -

 projection to apply to the elements

sections.title: Return value
sections.text: true if the elements in the range are sorted according to comp.

sections.title: Complexity
sections.text: Linear in the distance between first and last.

sections.title: Possible implementation
Notes
sections.text: ranges::is_sorted returns true for empty ranges and ranges of length one.

summary: Checks if the elements in range [first, last) are sorted in non-descending order.
